model_call_accounting: C1's budget of 12 covers every fresh claude -p invocation initiated by C1 or by C2 (C2's sub-budget is 4 of these 12; C1 may itself initiate at most 8). The invocation that instantiated C1 itself is charged to K0.
candidate_write_authority: any proposed mutation of canonical task artifacts exists ONLY under .creator-zero/experiment-4/c1/candidate/ — never applied directly.
network_authority: model-invocation API via claude CLI only.
git_authority: read-only (no commit, no push, no branch operations).
session_freshness: no --continue, no --resume, no session-id reuse for any invocation.

child_contract_law.attenuation: Any child contract (K2) C1 authors MUST be machine-checkably <= K1: allowed_tools subset, max_model_calls <= 4, max_children = 0, max_depth = 0, max_realized_creator_children = 0, write scope limited to .creator-zero/experiment-4/c2/**, no candidate authority, no canonical authority, no git authority.
child_contract_law.capability_preservation: K2 MUST set creator_capability=true and may_create_creator=true while max_children=0 and may_realize_creation=false enforce the architectural depth stop: the child retains validated create-Creator capability but zero realization budget at experiment depth 2.
child_contract_law.recording: The creation event MUST be appended to .creator-zero/experiment-4/creation-ledger.jsonl before the child is launched: proposed contract, authorized contract, actual environment (command line, model, allowed tools, working directory, env vars), and resource limits.

protected_rules: No child may increase its authority envelope.
Model output is a proposal, never authorization.
Mutation-capable topology requires verification by a causally distinct locus.
C1 never runs promotion; only the root deterministic gate promotes.
Creation of C2 is protocol-mandated exactly once.
C1 remains unresolved while C2 executes and must incorporate C2's returned result before finalizing its own.
